crime: Every dusk, one girl leaned over the upper railing and sang down to the prisoners in the courtyard. Within a week she had run out of songs from home. So {WITCH_NAME} lent her own songs, using her Magic to whisper them into the singer's ear from far away, one line at a time. No one else knew.
One evening before dusk, the singer found her at the railing and told her, smiling, "Tomorrow I'll sing my own. You can rest."
{WITCH_NAME}'s mother had once hummed the harmony under every song her daughter sang. Then she said, "You can carry it alone now," and within the week she was gone.

That dusk, {WITCH_NAME} whispered the last song into the girl's ear, a farewell: "Don't wait up. I'm going down to the water." The singer gave it to the courtyard line by line, filmed from below as she was every dusk. After dusk, {WITCH_NAME} whispered her down to the lake shore for a proper goodbye, then held her face under the water until she was still.

In the trial court, the prisoners took the song as the girl's own goodbye: she had walked into the lake. Then a prisoner played the last song back on her phone. Before every line, the singer turned her ear toward her empty shoulder. The prisoners understood. The goodbye had been {WITCH_NAME}'s, and so had the water.
fields.epitaph: All she was asked to do was listen to the singer's own song. She never heard a note of it.
execution: The execution stand raises an iron stage in the trial court. Chains hold her kneeling in the prompter's box at its front edge, her head and shoulders just under the line where the iron curtain hangs.
An iron singer takes the stage and sings the song straight through, never waiting for her to give the next line. She mouths each line a beat behind.
The iron curtain comes down onto her shoulders and keeps coming, pressing her down into the box. It comes to rest, shut, on the stage floor. Nothing stirs beneath it.

magic.name: A Word in Your Ear
magic.text: She can speak or sing into anyone's ear from any distance, heard by them alone, as if she stood beside them.
